gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She _____ reading a book when I called.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) for actions in progress at a specific time in the past.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She was reading a book when I called.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'By the time she arrived, I _____ already left.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past perfect (had + past participle) for actions completed before another past action.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: By the time she arrived, I had already left.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I _____ been waiting for an hour.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use present perfect continuous (have/has been + verb-ing) for actions that started in the past and continue to now.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I have been waiting for an hour.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'When I arrived, they _____ already finished dinner.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past perfect (had + past participle) to show an action completed before another past action.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: When I arrived, they had already finished dinner.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She _____ been living in London for three years before she moved.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past perfect continuous (had been + verb-ing) for actions that continued up to a point in the past.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She had been living in London for three years before she moved.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'You _____ have told me earlier!'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'should have + past participle' to express regret about past actions that didn't happen.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: You should have told me earlier!

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'You _____ borrow my book if you want.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'can' to express permission or ability.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: You can borrow my book if you want.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I _____ have done better if I had studied more.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'could have + past participle' to express past ability or possibility that didn't happen.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I could have done better if I had studied more.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'You _____ have been more careful!'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'should have + past participle' to express criticism or regret about past actions.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: You should have been more careful!

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'If I _____ known, I would have gone.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: This is a third conditional. Use 'had + past participle' in the if-clause for past hypothetical situations.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If I had known, I would have gone.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If she _____ call, tell her I'm busy.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'should' in first conditional to make it less likely or more formal. 'If she should call' means 'if by chance she calls'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If she should call, tell her I'm busy.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If I _____ rich, I would travel the world.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: This is a second conditional. Use 'were' (not 'was') for all subjects in hypothetical situations.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If I were rich, I would travel the world.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If I _____ you, I would have accepted the offer.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: This is a mixed conditional (past condition, present result). Use 'had been' in the if-clause.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If I had been you, I would have accepted the offer.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I need _____ hour to finish this.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound. 'Hour' starts with a vowel sound (silent 'h').
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I need an hour to finish this.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The building _____ built last year.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past tense 'was' (singular) or 'were' (plural) + past participle for passive voice in the past.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The building was built last year.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The book is _____ the table.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'on' for things that are in contact with a surface.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The book is on the table.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I'm interested _____ learning English.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'interested in' (not 'interested for' or 'interested about').
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I'm interested in learning English.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I _____ never been to Paris before.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use present perfect (have/has + past participle) with 'never' or 'ever' to talk about life experiences.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I have never been to Paris before.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'They _____ playing tennis when it started to rain.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) for actions in progress when another action happened.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: They were playing tennis when it started to rain.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: '_____ you help me with this, please?'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'Could' or 'Would' to make polite requests. 'Could' is common for asking favors.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: Could you help me with this, please?

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The cat is hiding _____ the bed.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'under' for things that are below or beneath something else.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The cat is hiding under the bed.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I will see you _____ Monday.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'on' for specific days of the week and dates.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I will see you on Monday.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The reason _____ she left is unknown.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'why' for reasons in adjective clauses. 'The reason' refers to a cause.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The reason why she left is unknown.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The book is _____, not yours.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'mine' (possessive pronoun) when there's no noun after it. 'My' is used before a noun.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The book is mine, not yours.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I _____ already seen that movie three times.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use present perfect (have/has + past participle) with 'already' to talk about completed actions.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I have already seen that movie three times.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'While I _____ cooking, the phone rang.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past continuous (was/were + verb-ing) for actions in progress when another action happened.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: While I was cooking, the phone rang.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I _____ have called you, but I forgot.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'should have + past participle' to express regret about past actions that didn't happen.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I should have called you, but I forgot.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'He _____ have arrived by now. The meeting started an hour ago.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'should have + past participle' to express expectation about past events that probably happened.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: He should have arrived by now. The meeting started an hour ago.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If I _____ you, I would accept the offer.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: This is a second conditional. Use 'were' (not 'was') for all subjects in hypothetical situations.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If I were you, I would accept the offer.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She is afraid _____ spiders.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'afraid of' (not 'afraid from' or 'afraid about').
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She is afraid of spiders.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I'm looking forward _____ seeing you.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'look forward to + -ing' (not 'look forward for').
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I'm looking forward to seeing you.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The day _____ we met was sunny.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'when' for time in adjective clauses. 'The day' refers to when something happened.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The day when we met was sunny.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She and _____ went to the store together.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use subject pronouns (I, you, he, she, we, they) when the pronoun is the subject of the sentence.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She and I went to the store together.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'By next year, I _____ living here for ten years.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use future perfect continuous (will have been + verb-ing) for actions that will have been ongoing up to a future time.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: By next year, I will have been living here for ten years.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'You _____ have told me earlier. Now it's too late.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'should have + past participle' to express regret or criticism about past actions.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: You should have told me earlier. Now it's too late.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If I _____ rich, I would buy a house.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: This is a second conditional. Use 'were' (not 'was') for all subjects in hypothetical situations.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If I were rich, I would buy a house.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She _____ been waiting for an hour when I arrived.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past perfect continuous (had been + verb-ing) for actions that were ongoing before another past action.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She had been waiting for an hour when I arrived.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I _____ have forgotten to lock the door. Let me check.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'might have' or 'could have' to express possibility about past events. 'Might' suggests less certainty.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I might have forgotten to lock the door. Let me check.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If you _____ me, I will help you.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: This is a first conditional. Use simple present in the if-clause.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If you ask me, I will help you.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She is responsible _____ the project.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'responsible for' (not 'responsible of' or 'responsible about').
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She is responsible for the project.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'They made the decision _____ themselves.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'by themselves' to mean 'alone' or 'without help'. 'Themselves' is a reflexive pronoun.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: They made the decision by themselves.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The book, _____ cover is torn, needs to be replaced.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'whose' to show possession in adjective clauses. 'Whose' can refer to both people and things.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The book, whose cover is torn, needs to be replaced.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The reason _____ I called you is important.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'why' for reasons in adjective clauses. 'The reason' refers to why something happened.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The reason why I called you is important.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I wanted to go to the party, _____ I had too much work.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'but' to show contrast between two ideas. 'But' connects contrasting clauses.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I wanted to go to the party, but I had too much work.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The students should do the homework _____.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use reflexive pronouns (myself, yourself, himself, herself, itself, ourselves, yourselves, themselves) when the subject and object are the same.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The students should do the homework themselves.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The company _____ I work is very large.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'where' for places in relative clauses. 'The company' refers to a place (location), so use 'where'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The company where I work is very large.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The new bridge _____ being built next year.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use future passive: 'will be + past participle'. 'Will be being' is not used; use 'will be + past participle' instead.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The new bridge will be built next year.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The day _____ I met you was the best day of my life.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'when' for time in adjective clauses. 'The day' refers to a time, so use 'when'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The day when I met you was the best day of my life.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I wanted to watch the movie, _____ I had to finish my homework first.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'but' to show contrast between what you want and what you must do.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I wanted to watch the movie, but I had to finish my homework first.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She cut _____ while cooking.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use reflexive pronouns when the subject and object are the same. 'She' cut 'herself'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She cut herself while cooking.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The restaurant _____ we had dinner was expensive.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'where' for places in relative clauses. 'The restaurant' refers to a location, so use 'where'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The restaurant where we had dinner was expensive.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: '_____ Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'the' with unique geographical features like oceans, seas, rivers, and mountain ranges.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The Pacific Ocean is the largest ocean.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The team _____ celebrating their victory.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: 'Team' can be singular (as a group) or plural (as individuals). Here it's treated as singular, so use 'is'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The team is celebrating their victory.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The problem _____ solved by the team yesterday.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past tense 'was' (singular) or 'were' (plural) + past participle for passive voice in the past.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The problem was solved by the team yesterday.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I will call you later,' she said. → She said that she _____ call me later.
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: In reported speech, 'will' becomes 'would'. Future tense changes to conditional.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She said that she would call me later.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She is afraid _____ spiders.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'afraid of' (not 'afraid from' or 'afraid about'). 'Of' follows 'afraid'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She is afraid of spiders.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She _____ have left already. Her car is gone.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'must have + past participle' to express a logical conclusion about a past event. The evidence suggests she left.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She must have left already. Her car is gone.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'If she _____ studied harder, she would have passed.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: This is a third conditional. Use 'had + past participle' in the if-clause for past hypothetical situations.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: If she had studied harder, she would have passed.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'By next year, I _____ living here for five years.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use future perfect continuous (will have been + verb-ing) for actions that will continue up to a future time.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: By next year, I will have been living here for five years.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The reason _____ she left is still unknown.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'why' for reasons in adjective clauses. 'The reason' refers to why something happened.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The reason why she left is still unknown.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The moment _____ I saw her, I knew she was special.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'when' for time in adjective clauses. 'The moment' refers to a time, so use 'when'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The moment when I saw her, I knew she was special.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'One should always do _____ best.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'one's' (possessive form of 'one') when using 'one' as a pronoun. 'One' is formal and singular.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: One should always do one's best.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I made this cake _____.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use reflexive pronouns when the subject and object are the same. 'I' made it 'myself'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I made this cake myself.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I like coffee, _____ my friend prefers tea.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'but' to show contrast between two different preferences or opinions.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: I like coffee, but my friend prefers tea.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: '_____ United States is a large country.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'the' with country names that are plural or include words like 'United', 'Kingdom', 'Republic'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The United States is a large country.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'She is _____ honest person.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'an' before words starting with a vowel sound. 'Honest' starts with a vowel sound (silent 'h').
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She is an honest person.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'Not only the teacher but also the students _____ excited.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: With 'not only...but also', the verb agrees with the subject closest to it. 'Students' is plural, so use 'are'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: Not only the teacher but also the students are excited.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The group of students _____ waiting outside.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: 'The group of' is singular, so use 'is'. The prepositional phrase 'of students' doesn't change the subject.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The group of students is waiting outside.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The report _____ written by the team last week.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use past tense 'was' (singular) or 'were' (plural) + past participle for passive voice in the past.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The report was written by the team last week.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The windows _____ cleaned every week.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use simple present passive: 'is/are + past participle'. 'Windows' is plural, so use 'are'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The windows are cleaned every week.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I'm leaving now,' he said. → He said that he _____ leaving then.
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: In reported speech, present continuous becomes past continuous. 'I'm leaving' becomes 'he was leaving'. Also, 'now' becomes 'then'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: He said that he was leaving then.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'I saw him yesterday,' she said. → She said that she _____ seen him the day before.
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: In reported speech, simple past becomes past perfect. 'I saw' becomes 'she had seen'. Also, 'yesterday' becomes 'the day before'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: She said that she had seen him the day before.

gap_fill_questions.prompt: Fill in the blank: 'The house _____ I grew up is now demolished.'
gap_fill_questions.explanationTemplate: Use 'where' for places in relative clauses. 'The house' refers to a location, so use 'where'.
gap_fill_questions.exampleSentence: The house where I grew up is now demolished.

transformation_questions.prompt: Convert to passive voice: 'The teacher explained the lesson.'

The lesson explained by the teacher.
The lesson was explained by the teacher.

transformation_questions.explanationTemplate: Use present perfect passive: 'has/have been + past participle'. 'Has stolen' becomes 'has been stolen'.

English is spoken all over the world.

choices.text: She said that I am tired.
She said that she was tired.
She said that she is tired.

transformation_questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: 'I will come tomorrow,' he said.

choices.text: She said that she can help me.
She said that she could help me.
She said that she will help me.

transformation_questions.prompt: Convert to passive voice: 'The chef cooked a delicious meal.'
transformation_questions.explanationTemplate: Passive voice: be + past participle. The object becomes the subject, and the original subject becomes optional (with 'by').

transformation_questions.explanationTemplate: Use present continuous passive: 'is/are being + past participle'. 'They are building' becomes 'A new school is being built'.

transformation_questions.prompt: Convert to reported speech: 'I have been waiting for an hour,' he said.
transformation_questions.explanationTemplate: In reported speech, present perfect continuous becomes past perfect continuous. 'I have been waiting' becomes 'he had been waiting'.
